topic: Two siblings inherit their grandmother's house
text: I never would have pegged that old house to end up in our hands. The will was read, and there we were, my brother and I, facing the weight of the place that had so many echoes of our childhood. The keys handed to us, the lawyer’s expectant gaze – as if we should spring into action, as if this wasn’t a mansion of memories, some more creaky and dusty than others. I suppose now we’re the guardians of this shrine to the past, whether we like it or not. The paperwork is just the beginning; the real challenge lies in what to do with all these rooms filled with a life that isn’t ours anymore.
